summary: Set 108 Session 2 of 4 wrote `docs/tutorials/three-module-pipeline.md` (1,445 lines), the four-part tutorial for the shape the product was designed around: several modules built independently and composed over agreed contracts. It holds S1's rulings R1-R9 as settled and quotes only literals. The session's distinguishing choice was to make literal fidelity MECHANICAL rather than a matter of care: the reference solution was re-run today (74 passing - 31/24/19 - plus the Phase A decision-table filter at 12 tests in 81 ms) and a checker extracts every wire-body and test-summary line from the tutorial and fails unless it appears verbatim in a provenance source (14/14 traceable). That checker caught a fabrication in the orchestrator's own first draft - a `Stored` transcript whose `fileName` had been edited to fit the prose while keeping the real `batchId` - which every literal around it made invisible to reading. The same evidence-first discipline settled two verification findings in OPPOSITE directions: a Major claiming `mkdir` at the root of `C:\` needs elevation and is not recursive was DISMISSED after a non-elevated probe showed both mechanisms false (the residual was still fixed, by removal - three mkdir lines became two), and a Major claiming Windows PowerShell 5.1 corrupts `curl ... > batch.json` was ACCEPTED after a probe returned first bytes `ff fe`, a UTF-16LE BOM that would have had readers debugging their own correct `persistence`. VERIFICATION: three rounds, closing VERIFIED with 0 findings and 3 accepted / 0 rejected fix verdicts. Ten distinct Majors across the two discovery rounds, all accepted, none disputed. Round 1's raw artifact was written but a 10-minute harness timeout killed the process before the findings envelope, and BOTH `--phase supplementary` and `--phase remediation-review` refuse to run without one; rather than hand-author a verification artifact (mixed-mode drift, forbidden), all six Majors were fixed once and `--phase discovery` was re-run on the corrected document - within the 2-pass bound, regenerating the envelope through the blessed writer, and a stronger check than the delta review it replaced. That decision paid immediately: round 2's top Major was a defect ROUND 1'S OWN REMEDIATION had introduced (the fix for a hard-coded batch id moved the capture into step 5, which meant step 5 re-ran `/run-now` after step 4 had already archived the only file, so the tutorial's final proof failed on the main path). It was caught independently during a coherence read before round 2 returned - the third time in this set that remediation introduced a fresh defect, against S1's four. The most instructive finding was structural rather than textual: Parts A and B assigned ports 5101/5102 in the day-one convention and probed them everywhere, but never ASKED for them in the build instructions and never passed `--urls` - so a completely correct `converter` would have failed every probe with nothing in the tutorial suggesting the port was the problem. Part D always used `--urls`, because running a second instance forces the question; the happy path never did, because it silently inherited the answer key's `appsettings.json`. Also fixed: the advertised solo path was internally inconsistent (told to use their own name, then told to declare nine modules for people who do not exist, with Part D offering only teammate commands), and Part C had no `What to build` section at all - it went from `build the logic and stub the services` straight to `now start everything`.

reason.specifics: Session 3 deletes `adopt-dabbler.md` Part 5 and nine video files and reconciles seven inbound linkers - a wrong deletion is the one class of mistake in this set that loses content permanently. It also inherits a hard ordering constraint from R4: before removing Part 5 it must confirm BY READING that the ownership-routing procedure (CODEOWNERS plus the Azure DevOps 'Automatically included reviewers' equivalent) actually exists in `three-module-pipeline.md`. A dead-link grep passes either way, so this is a content check, not a link check. S2 already de-risked one half of it: every remaining reference to `adopt-dabbler.md` is to Parts 1, 2-3, 3 or 4 - all of which survive the trim - and none uses a heading anchor, because S3 also strips seven '*(scene N)*' markers that any anchor would have depended on. The routed analyst recommended a cheaper tier, reasoning that S3 is precise editing rather than greenfield authoring; the reasoning is sound and the conclusion under-weights the irreversibility. Its named model (claude-3-sonnet-20240229) is not in this repo's catalogue at all, so the recommendation was restated on its merits rather than adopted. Second choice if the operator prefers provider diversity: openai / gpt-5-6, effort high.
